title: Corn Pudding
description:
We have always enjoyed Corn Pudding and Mommy would regularly make a recipe that we first did when we were living in the City. That’s the second one here and it’s more like a corn soufflé – delicious and delicate – but it requires a bit of work (though not too much).
Then, more recently, when Andrea wanted to do a chain-email recipe exchange, she got me involved (reluctantly on my part). No one responded, except Sue Mathias, who I used to work with at Trinity. And, she said she didn’t do this kind of thing! But, bless her heart, she sent me one of her family favorites. That’s the first recipe here.
Maybe because some of the ingredients come from a can or a box, it is wonderfully simple. But, it is also very tasty, especially for those tailgate or Super Bowl parties when you need a luscious dish to counterbalance all those ribs and chili and wings, etc. – not to mention beer and bourbon and margaritas, and who knows what else.
They both look pretty much the same coming out of the oven – tantalizing – and they are both wonderful!
Corn Pudding
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Melt the butter and combine with the rest of the ingredients in a baking dish.
Bake at 350 for about 40 minutes or until top and edges are getting brown and crusty.
That’s it!
Of course, you can “spice” it up (Mexican flavors?) or you can add vegetables (chopped onions, jalapeños, etc.?) or some meats (chorizo?), but the basic form is best. And, it’s easy to halve the recipe.
directions: Grease a round 10-inch baking dish, 2 ½ inches deep, with melted butter. Set aside.
Produce about 4 cups of corn, either frozen or by carefully slicing the corn kernels from the cob with a sharp knife.
Put half the corn kernels in a food processor with the eggs, half-and-half, flour, sugar, and a good shaking or grinding of salt and pepper.
Process for 4 or 5 seconds with a few on-and-off pulses, until roughly pureed. (Pureeing half the kernels, while leaving the remainder whole, gives the custard texture and body.)
Stir in the remainder of the kernels into the puree and pour into the prepared baking dish. Top with nutmeg and dot with soft butter.
Place baking dish in a pan and add enough hot water to come halfway up the sides of the baking dish. Bake for 1 hour or until a knife inserted into the center comes out clean.
Serve in the baking dish and enjoy!
This recipe came from Gene Hovis’s “Uptown Down Home Cookbook,” from our NYC days. He also introduced us to Cornish Hens!
